doc.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Upcoming plans and role models
summary: He lists concerts, a Museum of Modern Art Jackson Pollock-related show and symphony Pops plans, and credits Milt Hinton and Clark Terry as role models.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s up for you in the near future?

Well next week I go to three concerts in Raleigh, North Carolina in that area. And two weeks later out in Seattle, Washington for two more. I have a very interesting concert on January 1st at the Museum of Modern Art in New York in connection with the Jackson Pollock art exhibit that opens I think tomorrow on the first of November. And Jackson Pollock was a jazz fan and so they’re doing four Fridays in January. We’re doing it January 1st, the music that Jackson Pollock liked. Evidently he loved jazz and liked playing along while he painted. So whatever his bizarre paintings were you can blame jazz. But anyway we’re doing a thing called “A Night at Nick’s” which was the club that predated Condon’s with that great New York style jazz and it’s all based on his records, Jackson Pollock’s record collection. And I’m still working on I’ve got about eight or nine jazz festivals already booked or jazz parties for next year. I’m still trying hard to book us “The Magic of Swing Street” with symphony orchestras for Pops concerts, and continuing, just continuing on what we’ve been doing.
Well you can’t sit still, that’s for sure.

No, there’s no way. I mean I’ve had great role models in my life. Milt Hinton being one, Clark Terry being another. I shouldn’t even start naming names. I’ve had a lot of good role models that man, if you’ve been given this gift of being able to play and you like people, what better? It would take a couple of million dollars and maybe not even that to make me stop doing what I’m doing. Just, it’s a great way.
